titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Chariot Hidden, the Kings United (ch. 116–117)
part: ch. 116–117 — The Chariot Hidden, the Kings United
about: The Fathers ask whether Ethiopia's chariot will last until Christ's coming and are told it will be hidden. A prophecy follows of Rome and Ethiopia uniting, with Justin and Caleb meeting in Jerusalem, and of Caleb's two sons, Israel and Gabra Masqal, one given Zion and the other the hidden chariot. The Fathers confirm the vision and close the book's main narrative with a doxology.

sentences.t: ፻፲፮ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ሰረገላ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ።
sentences.l: 116. Concerning chariot Ethiopia
sentences.i: Chapter 116: Concerning the Chariot of Ethiopia
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፻፲፮ is 100 + 10 + 6 in Ethiopic numerals (there is no zero or place value). ሰረገላ is a wheeled vehicle, a chariot; the next word stands beside it as 'chariot (of) Ethiopia' with the construct linking left unmarked. What the 'chariot' stands for is the open question of this chapter (see the next units).

sentences.t: ወአውሥእዎ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ ሊቃነ ፡ ጵጳሳት ፡ ናሁኬ ፡ ነገርከነ ፡ በእንተ ፡ መግረሬ ፡ ፀር ፡ ዘሮሜ ፤
sentences.l: and-they-answered-him and-they-said-to-him chiefs-of bishops behold-then you-told-us concerning curb-of enemy of-Rome;
sentences.i: And the chief bishops answered him and said: So then, you have told us about the curb for the enemy, that of Rome (?).
sentences.n: The Fathers speak to the narrator. ወ- 'and' opens the narrative; አውሥእዎ is the causative of 'to answer', with the suffix -ዎ 'him', and ወይቤልዎ 'and they said to him' (ይቤሉ, 3mp perfect of the defective verb ብህለ, + -ልዎ 'to him'). ሊቃነ is the plural construct of ሊቅ 'chief' (construct: 'chiefs-of'); ጵጳሳት is the plural of ጳጳስ 'bishop' (from Greek). ናሁ 'behold' + the emphatic -ኬ, 'behold then', resuming what was said before. መግረሬ is the word of ch. 113 (ወመግረሬ ፀር), where it is the bit made from the nails of the cross; so 'curb' (?), in construct with ፀር 'enemy' (the root is not secure). ዘሮሜ: ዘ- 'of' + Rome, 'that of Rome'; it may qualify the curb (ch. 113 gives the curb to the king of Rome) or the enemy ('the enemy of Rome'), and I follow the first (?).

sentences.t: ወይእዜኒ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ሰረገላ ፡ ዘኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወእመሂ ፡ ይነብር ፡ ደኃሪ ፡ እስከ ፡ ምጽአተ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ከመ ፡ ነገርከነ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ወበእንተ ፡ ሃይማኖቶሙ ፡ ወከማሁ ፡ እመ ፡ ይነብር ፡ ሰረገላሆሙ ፡ ወይቤሎሙ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ሀለዎ ፡ ይሰወር ፤
sentences.l: and-now-also concerning chariot of-Ethiopia and-whether he-will-remain behind until coming-of Christ as you-told-us concerning Zion and-concerning faith-their and-likewise whether he-will-remain chariot-their and-he-said-to-them no it-is-fated-for-it he-be-hidden;
sentences.i: And now, about the chariot of Ethiopia: will it remain behind until the coming of Christ, as you told us about Zion and about their faith? And likewise, will their chariot remain? And he said to them: No. It must be hidden.
sentences.n: Here is the question that frames both chapters: the Fathers ask whether Ethiopia's 'chariot' (ሰረገላ) will last until Christ's coming. In ch. 113 the chariot is Zion itself (the Ark) in the Ethiopian king's keeping; here the two are asked about side by side ('as you told us about Zion') and in the next chapter they are set against each other, so I do not fix more than 'chariot' (?). ወይእዜኒ 'and now' (-ኒ is an emphatic enclitic). ዘኢትዮጵያ: ዘ- 'of'. እመሂ / እመ ('or whether', 'if') introduce the indirect question. ደኃሪ 'behind, afterward'. ከመ here is 'as', comparing with what he said of Zion. ሀለዎ ይሰወር: ሀለወ with a suffix means 'it is necessary / fated for him (it)', followed by a subjunctive, 'it must be hidden'. ይሰወር is the imperfect of ሰወረ 'hide'; the sense wanted is passive, 'be hidden' (one would expect the ተ- stem ይትሰወር, so the form is a little irregular (?)). The answer አልቦ 'there is not' = 'no' (to remaining visible).

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ስምዑኒ ፡ እንግርክሙ ፡ ሀለዎሙ ፡ ንስቲተ ፡ ያንሥኡ ፡ ርእሶሙ ፡ አይሁድ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ መሀይምናን ፡ በናግራን ፡ ወበአርማንያ ፡ እምድኅረዝ ፡ መዋዕል ፡ ወዘንተ ፡ ይገብር ፡ በፈቃዲ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ያኅልቆሙ ፤
sentences.l: and-again this hear-me that-I-tell-you it-is-fated-for-them a-little they-will-raise heads-their Jews against believers in-Najran and-in-Armenia after-this days and-this he-does by-will-of God that-he-destroy-them;
sentences.i: And again, hear me, that I may tell you this: for a little while they are bound to lift up their heads, the Jews, against the believers in Najran and in Armenia after these days. And this he does by the will of God, that he may make an end of them.
sentences.n: ስምዑኒ 'hear me' (2mp imperative + -ኒ 'me'; እንግርክሙ 'that I tell you' follows). ሀለዎሙ 'it is fated for them' again, with the subjunctive ያንሥኡ 'they raise'; ርእሶሙ 'their heads' is the idiom 'to lift the head' = to rebel, to grow bold. መሀይምናን 'believers' is a plural from the root of ሃይማኖት 'faith'. እምድኅረዝ 'after this' (-ዝ is a demonstrative, reduced from ዝ ). መዋዕል 'days' is the plural of ዕለት 'day'. በፈቃዲ is 'by the will of'; the ending -ዲ is irregular (ፈቃደ would be the construct), perhaps for 'his will' (?), but with እግዚኣብሔር following I take it as 'by the will of God'. ያኅልቆሙ is the causative of ኀልቀ 'to end', 'that he bring them to an end': 3ms verb + 'them' (a 3mp subject would be ያኅልቁሙ). Who 'he' is, in ይገብር and ያኅልቆሙ, is not said; God is the likeliest for the second (?). Najran is in southern Arabia (a historical place of Christian martyrdom under a Jewish king in the 6th century).

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ አርማንያ ፡ ደወለ ፡ ሮም ፡ ወናግራን ፡ ደወለ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: for Armenia region-of Rome and-Najran region-of Ethiopia
sentences.i: For Armenia is a region of Rome, and Najran is a region of Ethiopia.
sentences.n: እስመ 'for, because' gives the reason: both lands are dependencies of the two great Christian kingdoms. ደወለ is the construct of ደወል; I translate 'region' (it can also mean 'frontier, border'), so 'border-land of Rome' is also possible (?). The three ፨ at the end close the chapter.

sentences.t: ፻፲፯ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሮምያ ፡ ወንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ።
sentences.l: 117. Concerning king-of Rome and-king-of Ethiopia
sentences.i: Chapter 117: Concerning the King of Rome and the King of Ethiopia
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፻፲፯ = 117. ንጉሠ is the construct of ንጉሥ 'king': 'king-of Rome and king-of Ethiopia'. The form ሮምያ is a variant of the name of Rome, used in the heading; the text itself writes ሮም and ሮሜ (all one place).

sentences.t: ወይትለአኩ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሮምያ ፡ ወንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወሊቀ ፡ ጳጳሳት ፡ ዘእስክንድርያ ፡ ከመ ፡ ያኅልቅዎሙ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ርቱዕ ፡ ሃይማኖቶሙ ፡ ለሰብአ ፡ ሮም ፤
sentences.l: and-they-send-to-each-other king-of Rome and-king-of Ethiopia and-chief-of bishops of-Alexandria that-they-destroy-them while upright faith-their for-people-of Rome;
sentences.i: The king of Rome, the king of Ethiopia, and the chief bishop of Alexandria will exchange messages, so that they may destroy them, while the faith of the Romans is upright.
sentences.n: ይትለአኩ is the ተ- stem of ለአከ 'to send', here read as reciprocal, 'they send to one another' (the passive 'they are sent' is also possible (?)). ሊቀ ጳጳሳት 'chief-of bishops' is the title of the patriarch of Alexandria (the Ethiopian church's mother see). 'Them' (ያኅልቅዎሙ) is the Jews, named in the next unit. እንዘ ርቱዕ ሃይማኖቶሙ 'while straight their faith' is a circumstantial clause: Rome's faith is orthodox. ለሰብአ ሮም 'for the people of Rome': ለ- marks the possessor, a common Geʿez way to attach a noun to a preceding pronoun suffix ('their faith, belonging to the people of Rome').

sentences.t: ወይትነሥኡ ፡ ፀብአ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይጽብእዎሙ ፡ ለፀረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አይሁድ ፡ ወያኅልቅዎሙ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሮሜ ፡ ለኤንያ ፡ ወንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ለፊንሐስ ፡ ወያመዘብሩ ፡ ብሔሮሙ ፡ ወየሐንጹ ፡ አብያተ ፡ ክርስቲያናት ፡ በህየ ፡ ወየሐርድዎሙ ፡ ለነገሥተ ፡ አይሁድ ፡ በተፍጻሜተ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ ቀመር ፡ ፲ወ፪ ፡ አቅማር ።
sentences.l: and-they-rise-up war that-they-fight-them to-enemy-of God Jews and-they-destroy-them king-of Rome to-Enya and-king-of Ethiopia to-Phinehas and-they-lay-waste land-their and-they-build houses-of Christians there and-they-slaughter-them to-kings-of Jews at-completion-of this reckoning 12 reckonings.
sentences.i: They will rise up in war to fight them, the Jews, the enemies of God. The king of Rome, Enya, and the king of Ethiopia, Phinehas, will destroy them, and lay waste their land, and build churches there, and slaughter the kings of the Jews, at the completion of this reckoning of twelve reckonings (?).
sentences.n: ይትነሥኡ is the ተ- stem of ነሥአ 'to take', 'rise up'. ፀብእ 'war'; ከመ ይጽብእዎሙ 'that they fight them'. ለፀረ እግዚኣብሔር አይሁድ: 'the enemy-of God, the Jews' (ለ- marks the object, doubled by the suffix -ሙ on the verb, as with ለጽዮን in earlier parts). The word order in the next phrase is hard: ንጉሠ ሮሜ ለኤንያ ወንጉሠ ኢትዮጵያ ለፊንሐስ. I read ለ- before each name as the object/naming marker, 'king of Rome, Enya (?)' and 'king of Ethiopia, Phinehas'. Who these are I cannot say (?): they are not Justin and Caleb, who appear in the next unit. Phinehas is the biblical name (Numbers 25). አብያተ ክርስቲያናት 'houses-of Christians' = churches. ወየሐርድዎሙ: ሐረደ is 'to slaughter', the verb for killing animals, so the word is grim. ቀመር 'reckoning, computation, cycle' with ፲ወ፪ 'twelve' (ወ- 'and' between numerals, here ten-and-two) and the plural አቅማር: the phrase 'this reckoning, twelve reckonings' is obscure (?); I do not claim to know what period it measures.

sentences.t: አሜሃ ፡ ትትፌጸም ፡ መንግሥቶሙ ፡ ለአይሁድ ፡ ወትረትዕ ፡ መንግሥተ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ እስከ ፡ ምጽአተ ፡ ሐሳዌ ፡ መሲሕ ፡ ወእሙንቱሰ ፡ ነገሥት ፡ ዮስጢኖስ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሮሜ ፡ ወካሌብ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ይትራከቡ ፡ ክልኤሆሙ ፡ በኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ወይሠርዑ ፡ ቊርባነ ፡ ሊቀ ፡ ጳጳሳቲሆሙ ፡ ወይቄርቡ ፡ ወያኀብሩ ፡ ሃይማኖተ ፡ በፍቅር ፡ ወይትወሀቡ ፡ አምኃ ፡ ወሰላመ ፡ ወይትካፈሉ ፡ ምድረ ፡ እመንፈቃ ፡ ለኢየሩሳሌም ፡ በከመ ፡ ነገርነ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ርእሰ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ መጽሐፍ ፡ ቀዳሚ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ፍቅር ፡ ይዴመሩ ፡ ስመ ፡ መንግሥት ፡ ይዴመሩ ፡ ፩ ፡ ዘኀረዩ ፡ በሃይማኖት ፡ እምነገሥ ፡ ተ ፡ ሮም ፡ በውስተ ፡ ዕፃ ፡ ዘይሰመይ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወሰሎሞን ፡ አበዊሆሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይሰመይ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወንጉሠ ፡ ሮሜሂ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ይነሥእ ፡ ስመ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወይዴምር ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዕፃ ፡ ዘይሰመይ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ወሰሎሞን ፡ አበዊሆሙ ፡ በአምሳለ ፡ ፬ ፡ ወንጌላዊያን ፡ ወራብዕሰ ፡ ፩ ፡ ዘኀረዩ ፡ በበሀገሮሙ ፡ ወከመዝ ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ ኀብሩ ፡ ወአርትዑ ፡ ሃይማኖተ ፡ ይትማከሩ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢያሕይዉ ፡ አይሁድ ፡ ወየኀድጉ ፡ ህየ ፡ በበውሉዶሙ ፤
sentences.l: then it-will-be-fulfilled kingdom-their for-Jews and-it-will-be-upright kingdom-of Christ until coming-of false messiah and-those-ones-for-their-part kings Justin king-of Rome and-Caleb king-of Ethiopia they-meet two-of-them in-Jerusalem and-they-establish offering chief-of bishops-their and-they-draw-near and-they-unite faith in-love and-they-give-each-other gift and-peace and-they-divide land from-half-her to-Jerusalem as we-told in-beginning-of this book first and-again concerning love they-add name-of kingdom they-add 1 whom they-chose in-faith from-kings-of Rome in-wood which is-named with David and-Solomon fathers-their that he-be-named king-of Ethiopia and-king-of Rome-also likewise he-takes name-of king-of Ethiopia and-he-adds in-wood which is-named with David and-Solomon fathers-their in-likeness-of 4 evangelists and-the-fourth 1 whom they-chose in-each-their-lands and-thus after they-united and-made-upright faith they-take-counsel that not they-let-live Jews and-they-leave there each-with-their-sons;
sentences.i: Then the kingdom of the Jews will be brought to its end, and the kingdom of Christ will stand upright until the coming of the false messiah. As for those kings, Justin king of Rome and Caleb king of Ethiopia, the two of them will meet in Jerusalem. They will establish the offering of the chief of their bishops, and draw near, and unite in faith through love; they will give one another gifts and peace, and divide the land from its half, that of Jerusalem (?), as we said first at the beginning of this book. And again, concerning love: they will add the name of kingship. They will add one whom they have chosen in faith from the kings of Rome to the wood (?) that is named with David and Solomon, their fathers, so that he may be named king of Ethiopia. And the king of Rome likewise will take the name of king of Ethiopia and add it to the wood that is named with David and Solomon, their fathers, after the likeness of the four evangelists; and the fourth is one whom they chose, each in his own land (?). And after they have been united in this way and have set faith upright, they will take counsel not to let the Jews live, and each will leave his sons there (?).
sentences.n: This is a single very long unit (about a hundred words, over the usual ~45, but there is no ፤ or ። to cut at) because the source has no ፤ or ። inside it; I did not break it at the clause joints. ትትፌጸም is the passive of ፈጸመ 'to complete'; ትረትዕ 'will be straight' (ረትዐ, the verb of ርትዕ 'right, orthodox'; intransitive here, transitive in አርትዑ below). እሙንቱሰ: 'those' + -ሰ 'as for'. ሊቀ ጳጳሳቲሆሙ is 'chief of their bishops' (singular ሊቀ with the suffix on ጳጳሳት), the patriarch, not 'chief bishops'. ሐሳዌ መሲሕ 'false messiah' = the Antichrist. Justin (ዮስጢኖስ) is the Roman emperor, Caleb (ካሌብ) is Kaleb of Aksum (6th century, the conqueror of Himyar); history is compressed here. ወይሠርዑ ቊርባነ: ሠርዐ 'to establish, ordain', ቊርባን 'offering, the Eucharist'; ወይቄርቡ 'they take communion / draw near' (from the same root as ቊርባን). ምድረ እመንፈቃ ለኢየሩሳሌም: 'the land from its half' (-ሃ 'her/its' picked up by ለኢየሩሳሌም, the same anticipatory pattern as ለጽዮን); so half of Jerusalem's land, or half of it for each (?). 'As we said at the beginning of this book' points back to the division of the world between Rome and Ethiopia in the early chapters. The crux of the passage is the ዕፃ 'wood' (?) that is named with David and Solomon; ዕፀ is 'tree, wood'. It seems to be a document or a wooden tablet or staff on which the royal names are written, but that is my reading, not a certain one. The four 'names' imitate the four evangelists. In እምነገሥ ፡ ተ ፡ ሮም the source splits a word at the wrong place; read እምነገሥተ ሮም 'from the kings-of Rome' (an error of the digitization or the edition, retained as given). ይዴምር is ደመረ 'to add, join' (imperfect ይደምር), written here with ዴ. ተ- reciprocal ይትማከሩ 'they consult', from መከረ 'to counsel'. ኢያሕይዉ 'they do not let live' (causative of ሐይወ). በበውሉዶሙ 'among each their sons': በበ- is distributive; the meaning of the clause is uncertain (?).

sentences.t: ወንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያሰ ፡ የኀድግ ፡ ህየ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ዘበኵሩ ፡ ዘስሙ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወይገብእ ፡ ብሔሮ ፡ በፍሥሓ ፤
sentences.l: and-king-of Ethiopia-for-his-part he-leaves there son who-first-born-his whose-name Israel and-he-returns land-his in-joy;
sentences.i: As for the king of Ethiopia, he will leave there his firstborn son, whose name is Israel, and will return to his own land with joy.
sentences.n: -ሰ after ኢትዮጵያ ('king of Ethiopia-as-for') marks contrast. ዘበኵሩ is 'who (is) his firstborn'. ዘስሙ 'whose name' (ዘ- 'who' + ስሙ 'his name'). Israel is the elder son of Caleb in this story; ህየ 'there' is the place of the meeting (unit 8). Unit 12 later speaks of a king of Najran, son of Caleb, who may be this Israel (?). ይገብእ 'returns'. ብሔሮ 'his land'; በፍሥሓ 'in joy'.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ በጽሐ ፡ ቤተ ፡ መንግሥቱ ፡ ያአኵቶ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ ወይበጽዕ ፡ ሥጋሁ ፡ ለመሥዋዕተ ፡ ስብሐት ፡ ለአምላኩ ፤
sentences.l: and-when he-arrived house-of his-kingdom he-thanks to-God exceedingly and-he-offers(?) body-his for-sacrifice-of praise to-his-God;
sentences.i: And when he reaches his royal house, he thanks God greatly and offers his body (?) as a sacrifice of praise to his God.
sentences.n: ሶበ 'when'; ቤተ መንግሥቱ 'house-of his kingdom'. ያአኵቶ is 'he gives thanks' (the verb takes ለ for the one thanked). ይበጽዕ is uncertain (?): I read it as 'he brings, offers' (the root is not secure to me), parallel to the sacrifice of praise; the other possibility is an error for 'arrives'. The 'sacrifice of praise' echoes Psalm 50:14 and Hebrews 13:15 as a common phrase; the king offers himself in a spiritual sense.

sentences.t: ውጥቀ ፡ ይትወከፎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እስመ ፡ ኢያረኵስ ፡ ሥጋሁ ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ ገብአ ፡ አላ ፡ የሐውር ፡ ውስተ ፡ ደብር ፡ በንጹሕ ፡ ልብ ፤
sentences.l: exceedingly he-receives-it God for not he-defiles body-his after he-returned but he-goes into mountain in pure heart;
sentences.i: God receives it greatly, for he does not defile his body after he has returned, but goes to the mountain with a pure heart.
sentences.n: ውጥቀ is evidently a spelling of ወጥቀ 'exceedingly', and I take it so (?). ይትወከፎ is the ተ- stem ተወክፈ 'to receive, accept' with 'it' (the offering). ኢያረኵስ 'does not defile' (causative አርኰሰ of ረኰሰ 'be unclean'): he keeps himself chaste. ገብአ 'he returned' (perfect). 'The mountain' is a monk's retreat: he becomes an ascetic. በንጹሕ ልብ 'in pure heart' recalls Matthew 5:8 ('the pure in heart').

sentences.t: ወያነግሥ ፡ ወልዶ ፡ ዘይንእስ ፡ ዘስሙ ፡ ገብረ ፡ መስቀል ፡ ወውእቱሰ ፡ የዐጹ ፡ ርእሶ ፡ ወሶበ ፡ ነገርዎ ፡ ለንጉሠ ፡ ናግራን ፡ ወልደ ፡ ካሌብ ፡ ይመጽእ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይንግሥ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ወገብረ ፡ መስቀልኒ ፡ ያነሥእ ፡ ሰራዊተ ፡ ወየሐውር ፡ በሰረገላ ፡ ወይትራከቡ ፡ በኀበ ፡ መጽብበ ፡ ባሕረ ፡ ሊባ ፡ ወይትቃተሉ ፤
sentences.l: and-he-makes-king son-his the-young whose-name Servant-of Cross and-he-for-his-part he-shuts head-his(?) and-when they-told-him to-king-of Najran son-of Caleb he-comes that he-reign at Zion and-Servant-of Cross-also he-raises army and-he-goes with-chariot and-they-meet at narrows-of sea-of Liba and-they-fight;
sentences.i: And he makes his younger son king, whose name is Gabra Masqal (Servant of the Cross); and he himself shuts himself in (?). And when they told the king of Najran, the son of Caleb, he comes to reign where Zion is. And Gabra Masqal also raises an army and goes with the chariot, and they meet at the narrows of the sea of Liba, and fight.
sentences.n: ያነግሥ is the causative of ነግሠ 'to reign': 'he makes (his son) king'. ዘይንእስ 'who is young'. ገብረ መስቀል = 'servant-of the Cross' (the name is Gabra Masqal, the Ethiopian king of Aksum). የዐጹ ርእሶ is uncertain (?): ዐጸወ 'to shut' with ርእሶ 'his head / himself' suggests 'shuts himself in' (monastic enclosure), and I follow that; but the ending -ጹ looks like a 3mp, and ዐጸወ would be ይዕጽው, so both the root and the person are doubtful. The sentence about Najran is compressed: I take 'the king of Najran, son of Caleb' to be Israel, the elder son, who hears that his father has handed the kingdom to his brother and comes to claim Zion; this is my reading, not stated outright (?). ከመ ይንግሥ ኀበ ጽዮን 'that he reign at Zion'. -ኒ on ገብረ መስቀልኒ 'also'. ሰራዊተ 'army, host' (collective noun, accusative). መጽብብ 'narrow place, strait' (construct መጽብበ); ባሕረ ሊባ 'sea-of Liba' (Libya? the Red Sea? uncertain, I leave the name). ይትቃተሉ 'they fight one another' (reciprocal stem).

sentences.t: ወበአሐቲ ፡ ሌሊት ፡ ይጼልዩ ፡ ክልኤሆሙ ፡ እምሰርክ ፡ እስከ ፡ ነግህ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ጸንዖሙ ፡ ቀትል ፤
sentences.l: and-in-one night they-pray two-of-them from-evening until dawn when pressed-them battle;
sentences.i: And in one night the two of them pray, from evening until dawn, when the battle has pressed hard on them.
sentences.n: ይጼልዩ 'they pray' (the verb ጸለየ; the narrator uses the imperfect in a story told as prophecy). እምሰርክ እስከ ነግህ 'from evening to dawn'. ጸንዖሙ is ጸንዐ 'to be firm, to press' with 'them': 'the battle pressed them', 'was too strong for them'. ቀትል 'battle'.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ በከዩ ፡ ኀቤሁ ፡ በአንብዕ ፡ ይኔጽር ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ኀበ ፡ ጸሎተ ፡ ክልኤሆሙ ፡ ወጸሎተ ፡ አቡሆሙ ፡ ንሱሕ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ውእቱኒ ፡ መልህቅ ፡ ወቆመ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይግበር ፡ ፈቃደ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወለውእቱኒ ፡ መንእስ ፡ አፍቀሮ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ወጸለየ ፡ ኀበ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: and-when they-wept to-him with-tears he-looks God to prayer-of two-of-them and-prayer-of father-their penitent(?) while he-says he-also anchor and-he-stood that he-do will-of father-his and-as-for-that-also young he-loved-him father-his and-he-prayed to God;
sentences.i: And when they wept before him with tears, God looks upon the prayer of the two of them, and the prayer of their father, who is penitent (?), while he says, 'He too is an anchor (?)'. And he stood up to do the will of his father; and the young man too, his father loved him, and he prayed to God.
sentences.n: ኀቤሁ 'to him, before him'. ይኔጽር 'looks' (ነጸረ 'to look upon', here with favour); the prayer of their father is added as a second reason God hears. ንሱሕ is a hard word (?): from ነሰሐ (ንስሐ) 'to repent' (n-s-ḥ, with ሰ) would give 'penitent'; 'gentle' or 'humble' is also possible, and I have not checked Dillmann on it. The saying ውእቱኒ መልህቅ 'he also (is) an anchor' is obscure (?): መልህቅ is 'anchor', maybe as a figure for a firm support; I do not know who 'he' is. The next clause (ወቆመ 'and he stood') is read of the same son, 'to do his father's will'. -ኒ throughout is 'also, and'. አፍቀሮ 'loved him' (አፍቀረ + -ሆ): the object is the suffix and አቡሁ 'his father' is the subject (the accusative would be አባሁ), with ለውእቱኒ መንእስ 'as for him too, the young man' fronted and picked up by the suffix, as ለጽዮን elsewhere. So the father loves the son, and the son (ወጸለየ) prays.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ ለገብረ ፡ መስቀል ፡ ኅረይ ፡ ለከ ፡ እምሰረገላ ፡ ወእምጽዮን ፡ ወአፍተዎ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይንሣእ ፡ ጽዮንሃ ፡ ወይንገሥ ፡ ገሃደ ፡ ዲበ ፡ መንበረ ፡ አቡሁ ፤
sentences.l: and-he-said-to-him to-Servant-of Cross choose for-you from-chariot and-from-Zion and-he-allowed-him that he-take Zion-indeed and-he-reign openly upon throne-of father-his;
sentences.i: And he said to Gabra Masqal: 'Choose for yourself between the chariot and Zion.' And he allowed him to take Zion, and to reign openly on the throne of his father.
sentences.n: Here a voice speaks: God, or the father (not stated; I do not choose). አፍተዎ is 3ms (አፍተወ + -ሁ; a 3mp 'they' would be አፍተውዎ, as ነገርዎ above is 3mp), so it is the same single 'he' as ወይቤሎ. ኅረይ is the imperative of ኀረየ 'to choose'. ለከ 'for you' (a dative of interest). Choosing 'from the chariot and from Zion' sets two things against each other: Zion (the Ark, ታቦት) and the 'chariot'. ሰረገላ again carries the open question from ch. 116. አፍተዎ is አፍተወ 'to allow, grant the wish of' (?). ጽዮንሃ: -ሃ is an emphatic enclitic. ገሃደ 'openly'. መንበረ 'throne-of'.

sentences.t: ወለእስራኤልኒ ፡ አፍተዎ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይኅረይ ፡ ሰረገላ ፡ ወይንግሥ ፡ በኅቡእ ፡ ወኢይትረአይ ፡ ወይፌንዎ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ እለ ፡ ተዐደዉ ፡ ትእዛዘ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: and-to-Israel-also he-allowed that he-choose chariot and-he-reign in-secret and-not he-be-seen and-he-sends-him to all who transgressed commandment-of God;
sentences.i: And to Israel also he allowed to choose the chariot, and to reign in secret and not be seen, and he sends him to all who have broken the commandment of God.
sentences.n: The two brothers are given opposite lots: Gabra Masqal Zion and open kingship, Israel the chariot and hidden kingship. 'Hidden' answers the earlier answer, 'it must be hidden' (ch. 116). ይኅረይ is a subjunctive after ከመ. ኢይትረአይ 'and not be seen' (passive-reflexive of ርእየ). ይፌንዎ 'he sends him' (the sender unclear, again (?)). እለ ተዐደዉ 'who transgressed' (እለ 'those who'), ትእዛዘ 'the commandment-of'. The sense of the sending may be a punitive mission against those who break God's law (?).

sentences.t: ወአልቦ ፡ ዘየሐንጽ ፡ አብያተ ፡ ወይነብር ፡ በደብተራት ፡ ወአልቦሙ ፡ ጻማ ፡ ዘስራሕ ፡ ወኢጻማ ፡ በፍኖት ፤
sentences.l: and-there-is-not who builds houses and-he-dwells in-tents and-there-is-not-to-them toil of-work and-not toil on-road;
sentences.i: And there is no one who builds houses, but he dwells in tents; and they have no toil of work and no toil on the road.
sentences.n: Describes the people of the chariot: a nomadic, burden-free life. አልቦ ዘ- 'there is no one who'. ደብተራት 'tents' (cf. the tabernacle, ደብተራ). አልቦሙ 'there is not to them' = 'they have not'. ጻማ 'toil, labour'. ፍኖት 'road, way'.

sentences.t: ወመዋዕሊሆሙኒ ፡ ካዕበተ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ወከመዝኬ ፡ የህይጲ ፡ ወይዌስቁ ፡ ወይወግኡ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዘጸልኦ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ።
sentences.l: and-days-their-also double-of people and-thus they-prosper(?) and-they-increase(?) and-they-strike toward whom hated God.
sentences.i: And their days are double those of other people; and so they prosper (?) and increase (?), and they strike those whom God hates.
sentences.n: መዋዕሊሆሙ 'their days'. ካዕበተ ሰብእ 'double-of people': either 'twice the life of men' or 'a second people' (?). የህይጲ is uncertain (?): I read 'they flourish'. ይዌስቁ 'they increase' (?): I take it from ወሰከ 'add', but the final radical here is ቁ (q), not ከ (k), so the root is not secure. ይወግኡ 'they strike' (ወገአ). ኀበ ዘጸልኦ እግዚኣብሔር 'toward the one whom God hates' (ጸልአ 'to hate'). The ። here ends the narrated prophecy.

sentences.t: ከመዝ ፡ ገብረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ክብረ ፡ ወሞገሰ ፡ ወዐብየ ፡ እምኵሎሙ ፡ ነገሥተ ፡ ምድር ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዕበያ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ሰማያዊት ፤
sentences.l: thus did God to-king-of Ethiopia glory and-favour and-he-became-great beyond all kings-of earth for greatness-of-her to-Zion ark-of his-law of-God Zion heavenly;
sentences.i: So God did for the king of Ethiopia: glory and majesty, and he grew great beyond all the kings of the earth, for the greatness of Zion, the ark of the law of God, heavenly Zion.
sentences.n: ከመዝ 'thus, so'. ሞገስ 'favour, grace, majesty'. ዐብየ is 'was/became great' (G perfect, intransitive; the causative would be አዕበየ), with the king as its subject. በእንተ ዕበያ ለጽዮን 'on account of her greatness, to Zion' (the pronoun -ያ is anticipatory; ለ- then names the owner). ታቦተ ሕጉ ለእግዚኣብሔር 'ark-of his law, God's': the ark of the covenant, the central theme of the book. ጽዮን ሰማያዊት 'heavenly Zion' sets the earthly Ark alongside the Zion of heaven (see Hebrews 12:22).

sentences.t: ወይረስየነ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ንግበር ፡ ሥምረቶ ፡ መንፈሳዊተ ፡ ወያድኅነነ ፡ እመዐቱ ፡ ወይከፍለነ ፡ መንግሥቶ ፡ አሜን ፨
sentences.l: and-he-makes-us God that we-do pleasure-his spiritual and-he-saves-us from-his-wrath and-he-gives-share-to-us kingdom-his amen
sentences.i: May God make us do his spiritual pleasure, and save us from his wrath, and give us a share in his kingdom. Amen.
sentences.n: A blessing by the narrator. ይረስየነ 'he makes us' (ረሰየ), followed by ከመ and a subjunctive. ሥምረት 'pleasure, good will'; መንፈሳዊተ 'spiritual' (feminine accusative). ይከፍለነ 'gives us a portion' (ከፈለ 'to divide'), with a double object. The verbs are imperfects used as a wish (jussive sense).

sentences.t: ወአውሥኡ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ በአማን ፡ ሠናየ ፡ ነበብከ ፡ እስመ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ተከሥተ ፡ ለከ ፡ በረድኤተ ፡ መንፈስ ፡ ቅዱስ ፤
sentences.l: and-they-answered and-they-said-to-him in-truth well you-spoke for thus it-was-revealed to-you by-help-of Spirit Holy;
sentences.i: And they answered and said to him: Truly you have spoken well, for it was revealed so to you by the help of the Holy Spirit.
sentences.n: The Fathers reply. በአማን 'in truth'. ተከሥተ is the passive of ከሠተ 'to reveal': 'was revealed'. ረድኤት 'help'; መንፈስ ቅዱስ 'Spirit Holy' (adjective after noun, Geʿez order).

sentences.t: ነገርከነ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ዘኮነ ፡ ወአኅበርከ ፡ ምስለ ፡ መጽሐፈ ፡ ደማቲዮስ ፡ ዘሮሜ ፡ ወተነበይከ ፡ ለነ ፡ ዘይከውንሂ ፡ ለክልኤ ፡ አህጉር ፡ መራዕወ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ አብያተ ፡ ክርስቲያናት ፡ ንስታስያ ፡ ወአርቃድያ ፡ ወማሬና ፡ ወኢትዮጵያ ፡ አህጉር ፡ ዐበይት ፡ ዘእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ዘበውስቴቶን ፡ መሥዋዕተ ፡ ወቊርባነ ፡ ንጹሕ ፡ ይትገበር ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ጊዜ ።
sentences.l: you-told-us everything what happened and-you-joined with book-of Demetrius of-Rome and-you-prophesied to-us what will-be-also for-two cities pasture-of(?) Christ houses-of Christians Anastasia and-Arcadia and-Marina and-Ethiopia cities great of-God in-which sacrifice and-offering pure is-done at all time.
sentences.i: You have told us everything that happened, and joined it with the book of Demetrius of Rome, and prophesied to us what will be for the two cities, the pasture (?) of Christ: the churches (?) Anastasia, Arcadia and Marina, and Ethiopia, great cities of God, in which a pure sacrifice and offering is made at all times.
sentences.n: አኅበርከ 'you joined' (causative of ኀብረ 'to unite'). Demetrius of Rome is some earlier book (ደማቲዮስ), referred to as a known book; I cannot say more (?). ይከውንሂ 'what will be, also'. ለክልኤ አህጉር 'for two cities/lands' (ክልኤ 'two', አህጉር plural of ሀገር). መራዕወ is uncertain (?): from the root ርዕየ 'to pasture', so 'pasture of Christ'; the ending -ወ is unexplained (?). ንስታስያ ወአርቃድያ ወማሬና look like Greek-derived names (Anastasia, Arcadia, Marina); whether they name churches, lands or persons I cannot decide, and these are in the text transliterated. ዐበይት 'great (plural)'. ዘበውስቴቶን: ዘ- 'which' + በ- + ውስተ 'inside' + -ቶን '3fp them': 'in the inside of them' (the cities, feminine plural). መሥዋዕት 'sacrifice', ቊርባን 'offering/Eucharist'; ንጹሕ 'pure' recalls Malachi 1:11 ('a pure offering in every place').

sentences.t: እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይጸግወነ ፤
sentences.l: God he-grants-us;
sentences.i: May God grant us
sentences.n: ይጸግወነ 'may he grant us' (ጸገወ, jussive). The sentence runs on into the next unit: the blessing of the saints is what he grants.

sentences.t: በረከቶሙ ፡ ለኵሎሙ ፡ ቅዱሳን ፡ ወሰማዕት ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ንጉሥነ ፡ ወበክርስቶስ ፡ ሕይወትነ ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፡ ወአሜን ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: blessing-their of-all saints and-martyrs for-age-of age amen Christ king-our and-in-Christ life-our for-age-of age amen and-amen
sentences.i: the blessing of all the saints and martyrs, for ever and ever. Amen. Christ is our king, and in Christ is our life, for ever and ever. Amen and amen.
sentences.n: A closing doxology. በረከቶሙ 'their blessing' (the blessings of the saints, with a pronoun anticipating ለኵሎሙ ቅዱሳን 'of all saints'). ሰማዕት 'martyrs' (literally 'witnesses'). ለዓለመ ዓለም 'for age-of age' = for ever and ever (a doubled construct, as in the Greek). አሜን ወአሜን 'amen and amen'. The line of ፨ marks at the end close the last chapter of the main story; the colophon follows as a separate part.
